notes: This is the causal-mechanism graph the reasoning engine walks. Each edge names a directional ecological relationship between two tracked variables, in plain language, with a pointer to which knowledge_base.json ids substantiate it. The reasoning engine never invents a new edge at answer time - it can only cite edges declared here, which keeps 'multi-metric reasoning' auditable instead of an LLM improvising causal claims.

edges.relationship: Soil organic carbon feeds microbial and invertebrate communities directly and improves plant productivity indirectly, raising the resource base that supports higher trophic diversity.
Rainfall is the primary input to soil moisture; low or erratic rainfall directly lowers moisture availability, especially in semi-arid soils with low organic carbon (which hold less water).
Soil moisture constrains which plant and soil-faunal species can survive at a site; chronic moisture stress filters out moisture-sensitive species, narrowing richness.
Converting structurally complex land cover (forest, agroforestry, mixed cropping) to uniform monoculture removes vertical and horizontal habitat structure that many species depend on.

More structurally and compositionally diverse habitat supports more ecological niches, generally supporting more species - though the effect of patch fragmentation specifically (as opposed to habitat amount) is scientifically contested.

Continuous monoculture with bare-soil periods depletes soil organic carbon over time; cover cropping, intercropping, or agroforestry keeps living roots in the ground and adds residue, building carbon back up.
Removing woody/perennial vegetation eliminates structural habitat layers and increases edge exposure and erosion, degrading remaining habitat quality even where some vegetation remains.

Nutrient and sediment pollution reduce usable clean water and can trigger algal blooms that further degrade aquatic habitat quality; vegetated buffers intercept this pollution before it reaches waterways.
Clean, adequate water availability is a baseline requirement for aquatic and riparian species; pollution or scarcity directly filters which species can persist.
Higher temperatures increase evapotranspiration, drawing down soil moisture faster for a given amount of rainfall, compounding drought stress in already low-rainfall regions.
Extreme soil pH suppresses microbial and root activity, slowing the biological processes that build and stabilize soil organic carbon.
Soil organic carbon improves soil aggregate structure and water-holding capacity, so higher SOC lets a soil retain more plant-available water from a given rainfall event.
